newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank merger policy should be re-examined - RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank merger policy should be re-examined - RBA.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said on Monday it supported calls for a fresh look at the nation's "six pillars" policy which prevents mergers among Australia's largest banks and life offices.

"On competition policy, the RBA believes that the same broad principles which are used to evaluate mergers in other industries should be used to evaluate mergers in the financial services sector," the central bank said in its submission to the government's Wallis Inquiry into the financial system.
"This would mean taking a fresh look at the "six pillars" policy which prevents mergers between any of the four largest banks and the two largest life offices," the RBA said.
"The "four plus one" interpretation of the Trade Practices ACt, whereby a regional bank presence is required in each State, should also be examined," it said.

The Wallis Inquiry, which required all submissions to have been lodged by Monday, is due to hand its report to the government by March next year. Industry deregulation is a key topic under consideration but the government has opposed any industry mergers during the life of the inquiry.

The current merger policy was set by the former Labor government which opposed a strategic link between the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and the National Mutual Life Association of Australasia Ltd. It was subsequently widened to block any mergers between the four major banks or with the two life offices, the AMP Society and National Mutual.

The other major banks, which have operations in each of the six states, are National Australia Bank Ltd, Westpac Banking Corp, and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia. While it supported a re-examination of finance industry mergers, the RBA was cautious about inter-bank mergers.
"It would be a much more serious step, however, to redefine competition policy in a way which effectively reduced the number of major banks in Australia to two," the RBA said.
Analysts have speculated that a completely deregulated marketplace could see National Australia bidding for ANZ or Westpac.
Separately, the RBA continued its opposition to the formation of a "mega-regulator" which would oversee banks, life and superannuation offices, and building societies.
